## Natural history notes

A small acrobat ant characterized by its reddish-brown to dark body, slender waist, and heart-shaped abdomen that can be raised over the body when disturbed. In Florida, it is associated with pine-dominated habitats such as pine flatwoods, sandhills, open pine woodlands, forest edges, and wooded yards where pines, dead twigs, bark crevices, or plant cavities provide nesting sites. It forages on trees and low vegetation for small insects, nectar, honeydew, and other sugary resources, while nesting in hollow twigs, dead branches, or cavities and serving as prey for spiders, birds, lizards, and other insect-eating animals.
